system_overview: This is a model-checking configuration module for the TCP connection state machine specification. It extends the TCP specification and provides a restricted initial state and action constraints that make the state space finite and amenable to exhaustive model checking. Instead of starting from the CLOSED state, one peer begins in SYN-SENT (having already performed an active open) and the other begins in LISTEN (having already performed a passive open), with the corresponding SYN segment already in flight.
actors_and_components: Same as the TCP specification: exactly two peers communicating over ordered network queues. This module names the two peers as specific constants and defines a symmetry set for them.
state_variables: Inherits all state variables from the TCP specification. No additional state variables are introduced.
initial_state: One peer starts in SYN-SENT and the other in LISTEN, both with their transmission control blocks created. The listening peer's network queue contains a single SYN segment (the one sent by the active opener). The active opener's queue is empty. This models a scenario where one active open and one passive open have already occurred.
actions: Inherits all actions from the TCP specification, with two additional constraints: (1) A no-retransmission constraint prevents consecutive identical messages in any peer's network queue. (2) A single-active-open constraint prevents any further active open, passive open, or send user commands, since the initial open is already accounted for in the initial state. These constraints bound the state space to make model checking feasible.
safety_properties: Inherits from the TCP specification: connection state consistency (when no messages are in flight and one peer is established, the other must also be established) and type correctness.
liveness_properties: Inherits from the TCP specification: a peer in SYN-SENT eventually reaches ESTABLISHED, LISTEN, or CLOSED.
model_bounds: The two peers are instantiated as specific named constants. Symmetry reduction over the two peers is defined but commented out (must be disabled for liveness checking). The initial state constrains one peer to SYN-SENT and the other to LISTEN. Action constraints prevent additional connection opens and message retransmission to keep the state space finite.
additional_assumptions: This module is designed for model checking only. It assumes exactly one connection lifecycle starting from a specific point (one active open already completed). The no-retransmission constraint and single-active-open constraint are modeling simplifications to ensure finite state exploration. Symmetry reduction is available but must be disabled when checking liveness properties.
